candidates.statement: There is a transitive action on the Weierstrass points on a compact Riemann surface X of genus g > 2 and the Weierstrass points are simple if and only if one of the following statements holds. (1) g = 4 and X is isomorphic to Bring’s curve. (2) g = 3 and X ∈K3 is isomorphic Ct for some t diﬀerent from 0 and 3. RIEMANN SURFACES WITH TRANSITIVE ACTION ON WEIERSTRASS POINTS The theorem above answers a question posed by Laing and Singerman and com- pletes [24, Theorem 15]. For the sake of completeness, we recall that the Weierstrass points of Bring’s curve were found by Edge in [9]; see also [2, Section 3.1].

candidates.statement: The Weierstrass points of Fermat’s quartic were obtained by Hasse in [13]. Besides, the Weierstrass points of C3 can be easily computed, since they are the ﬁxed points of the involutions conjugate to [x : y : z] 7→[−x : y : z]. Explicitly, the Weierstrass points of C3 are [0 : 1 : ζ], [1 : ζ : 0], [ζ : 0 : 1] where ζ = ± q −3± √ . As simple Weierstrass points are precisely ordinary ﬂexes, the Weierstrass points of Ct for t̸ = 0, −1, ±2, 3, t0 are the points of Ct at which the Hessian determinant vanishes.
